text:
[verdict]
In the 50 retrieved historical episodes where the tape looked like NVDA on 2026-09-18, the realised 5-session returns were slightly positive on balance, with a median of 0.86% and a mean of 0.65%. The single number to anchor on is the dispersion: the standard deviation across those 50 outcomes was 3.8%, meaning the path over one trading week routinely swung several percent in either direction. This is a description of a historical conditional distribution, not a forecast or a recommendation to open or avoid a position.

[state]
The engine selected these analogs because the current state is defined by a specific combination of features. NVDA is sitting -6.03% from its 52-week high (dist52), which places it near but not at the absolute peak. Its own 20-session realised volatility (vol20) is elevated at 45.77%, while the benchmark 20-session volatility (mktVol20) is unusually quiet at 9.16%. That divergence—high idiosyncratic vol against a calm market—is a primary driver of the retrieval. The macro backdrop includes a sharp WTI crude change over 20 days (oilChg20) of 19.24%, the most extreme z-score in the feature set at 1.124. Liquidity conditions are softer than average, flagged by a 20-session dollar-volume regime z-score (dv20z) of -0.785. Finally, there are 45 calendar days to the next earnings release (dte) and 0 scheduled events in the next 5 sessions (eventLoad5). The name-weighting block (30% of the distance metric) pulls in other Technology names, while the macro block (20%) matches episodes with similar oil and rate dynamics.

[history]
Over the 5-session horizon, the 50 analogs produced a median return of 0.86% and a mean of 0.65%. The spread is wide: the 10th percentile was -4.04%, the 25th percentile was -2.03%, the 75th percentile was 3.07%, and the 90th percentile was 4.68%. The extremes ranged from a minimum of -7.34% to a maximum of 10.25%. In 56% of the episodes the 5-session return was above 0%, and in 44% it was below 0%. The histogram shows the bulk of outcomes clustered between -1.85% and 3.29%, with a slight positive skew of 0.214.

The bad tail is dominated by specific episodes. The closest analog in the entire library is NVDA itself on 2026-09-08 (distance 0.2999), which went on to realise a 5-session return of -5.9%. Another Technology analog, XLK on 2026-08-13 (distance 0.4178), returned -4.02%. On the upside, a prior NVDA episode on 2025-06-20 (distance 0.4317) returned 9.66%, and MU on 2024-01-16 (distance 0.4111) returned 3.45%. The retrieval spans from 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08, drawing from 31 distinct sessions and 33 distinct symbols, with only 3 same-symbol matches for NVDA.

[tails]
A position can finish the week near flat and still be difficult to hold through the intra-week path. Across the 50 analogs, the median max adverse excursion was -2.01%. At the 25th percentile, the worst drawdown during the 5 sessions reached -3.77%, and at the 10th percentile it reached -4.38%. Conversely, the median max favourable excursion was 2.55%, reaching 4.39% at the 75th percentile and 6.71% at the 90th percentile. The reward-risk ratio computed from these excursions is 1.27.

For specific drawdown thresholds, the probability of breaching a 5% drawdown at any point during the 5 sessions was 8 out of 50 episodes. The probability of breaching a 10% drawdown was 0 out of 50, as was the probability for 15% and 20% drawdowns. The conformal interval, scaled to target 80% coverage, runs from -4.12% to 5.83%, a total width of 9.95%.

[stress]
The stress scenarios that materially worsen the baseline median of 0.65% are led by the 2020-02/03 liquidity crash window. There, the median 5-session return was -5.4%, a delta of -6.26% versus baseline, and the 10th percentile reached -14.14%. The probability of falling below -10% was 20.8%, and the probability of breaching a 10% drawdown intra-horizon was 58.3%. Caveat: central-bank backstops arrived inside the window, so the realised rebound is baked into the forward returns; it is a sample of one regime, not a forecast of the next one.

The 2018-Q4 tightening scare produced a median return of -3.02% (delta -3.88%), with the 90th percentile at -0.19%, meaning almost no upside in that regime. Caveat: it ended with a policy pivot in January 2019, which flatters the forward returns of late-window analogs. The 2022 inflation/rate bear scenario showed a median of -2.42% (delta -3.28%). Caveat: a nine-month window means the per-date cap of 2 analogs samples it repeatedly; treat it as a regime description, not 50 independent events. The 2024-08-05 carry unwind had a median of -2.11% (delta -2.97%). Caveat: reversal was almost as fast as the drawdown, so H-day forward returns look benign even though the intra-horizon excursion did not. The 2025-04 tariff shock yielded a median of -2.7% (delta -3.56%). Caveat: policy reversals inside the window make the tail of the distribution asymmetric in a way that is specific to that episode.

Among the shock scenarios, a +2 sigma VIX spike produced a median of -0.18% (delta -1.04%). Caveat: VIX shocks mean-revert quickly, so this stresses entry timing more than terminal value. A liquidity air pocket had a median of 0.83% (delta -0.03%). Caveat: gap20 is measured on the underlying exchange session, not on a 7x24 venue, bounding reference-market gap risk only. The remaining scenarios (regional banks 2023, rates-up, earnings-day, FOMC-day, crypto contagion, China ADR de-rating) produced medians ranging from -0.39% to 1.61%, none worsening the baseline by more than -1.25%. No scenarios were skipped by the engine.

[limits]
This analysis has concrete limits. The engine's own validation states explicitly: "Analog retrieval hits its coverage target out of sample and its width tracks each instrument's own volatility, but it is NOT sharper than a same-name unconditional band at matched coverage, and its raw PIT distribution fails a uniformity test. It is a stress-testing and provenance instrument, not an alpha source." The directional hit rate is 50.1%, meaning the retrieval does not reliably predict the sign of the next week's return better than a coin flip. The matched coverage sharpness versus the same-name unconditional benchmark is -7.6%. The PIT chi-square statistic is 208.6, far above the 5% critical value of 16.92, confirming the raw probability integral transform fails uniformity.

Only 3 of the 50 retrieved analogs are NVDA itself; the rest are cross-sectional matches from 33 distinct symbols, meaning the idiosyncratic behaviour of NVDA is heavily diluted by sector and macro proxies. The retrieval relies on 31 distinct sessions spanning 2016-12-14 to 2026-09-08. Bitget endpoints were unreachable during the build (TCP connection reset), so no Bitget-sourced figures are present. Earnings dates for foreign private issuers are derived from 6-K full-text search and are noisier than domestic 8-K filings. Every stress scenario carries its own caveat, detailed above, preventing any of them from being treated as a clean probability of future loss.
